axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Jira/Confluence capabilities
(searching issues, reading and writing pages, querying projects) as tools for agents.
axes.runtime: An official hosted remote server (product page direct-fetched 200); a single endpoint covers both the Jira and Confluence product surfaces.
axes.local_files: Never touches the local file system — the scope is Atlassian cloud sites (issues, pages).
axes.background: The service lives on Atlassian's side; request-response semantics, no background tasks.
axes.tools:
Jira: search/read/create/update issues, query projects; Confluence: search/read/create/update pages.
The complete inventory follows the official docs; it has not been enumerated item by item.
axes.context: No server-side cross-session memory — state lives on the sites themselves.
axes.permissions:
OAuth 3LO user authorization: the agent-visible surface = the connected account's permissions on the site (including project-level restrictions);
write capabilities (creating issues / editing pages) take effect directly — defend on the assumption "it can edit your wiki for you".
axes.fit:
Fits: agents in enterprise dev flows pulling Jira requirement context and writing Confluence docs.
Not a fit: scenarios needing write-approval flows; Data Center self-hosted support status is unverified.

mcp.transport:
**Streamable HTTP remote hosting** (official endpoint); verified: product page 200 (2026-10-21).
The concrete endpoint URL follows the official docs (not verified item by item).
mcp.auth: OAuth 3LO (user login authorization); scopes are split by product (separate scope families for Jira / Confluence).
mcp.scope:
Read surface: issue/page search and reading; write surface: create/update issues, create/update pages.
It follows the account's permissions; there is no tool-level approval layer.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The endpoint URL and the full scope table (not verified item by item)
- Data Center support status (no official statement seen)
- The complete tool inventory (not enumerated item by item)
related: Also an issue-management server: Linear is lightweight single-product; Atlassian is one endpoint for two products with a heavier enterprise permission surface.
